title: Follow-the-arrow physical route signs
central_assumption: A continuous, symbol-led sign trail can lead visitors from the south gate along the documented paved step-free route to West Canopy without a phone, while keeping them off the lawn shortcut. Shade at West Canopy is not established by its name and must be verified before this route can satisfy the shaded-refill brief.
proposal: Design a temporary family of physical directional signs: a large water symbol, a prominent arrow, the destination name, and a consistent step-free route cue. Begin at the south gate, repeat at each actual route choice on the paved path, and place a confirmation sign at the refill point. At the lawn split, direct visitors along the paved route and explicitly mark the lawn shortcut as not step-free. Use a replaceable paper hours panel only after operating hours are decided; otherwise omit hours and make no evening-service claim. Do not print 'shaded refill' until on-site shade at the staffed destination is checked. First map the exact sign positions, test them with visitors including wheelchair users, obtain placement permission, and price fabrication, installation, daily upkeep, and removal against the full £8,000 cap. This is a concept for decision, not an approved installation.
dependencies: Verify by observation that West Canopy actually offers shade during relevant refill hours. Its name is not evidence of shade. If it does not, this destination does not satisfy the brief and the route choice must be revisited.
Survey the paved route's real decision points and secure sign placement permissions; neither positions nor permissions are established in the packet.
Get a complete quote or costed plan showing fabrication, placement, upkeep, and removal within the £8,000 cap; total cost is unverified.
Decide refill-point operating hours before printing any hours or evening-service statement; hours remain unverified.
Obtain management approval before installation; the operations note says no design has been approved.
risks: A missing or misplaced sign at one junction could steer visitors onto the non-step-free lawn shortcut.
The water symbol and arrow were mentioned by four visitors, but comprehension of this particular sign system has not been tested.
A once-morning paper update cannot reflect a closure later the same day without an additional operating rule.
West Canopy might not provide shade when visitors need it; no supplied source verifies shade there.
Signs could exceed the pilot cap once placement and removal are included, or lack permission at necessary locations.
rough_effort: One route walk to identify decision points, a small physical sign mockup and visitor navigation trial, followed by permission and full-cost checks before any production decision. No duration or price estimate is established.
falsifying_test: Give first-time visitors, including wheelchair users, only the proposed physical signs from the south gate. Reject or revise the design if they take the lawn shortcut, cannot identify the paved step-free route and staffed refill point without a phone, or mistake the signs for a promise of shade or evening opening that has not been verified. Independently reject this destination if a site check does not confirm usable shade during the intended service period.
